unmapped: Actions are assortments S of at most K of N items; feedback is the index of a single chosen item (or the outside option 0) drawn from an MNL choice model p_i(S)=v_i/(1+sum_{j in S} v_j)
Expected reward of assortment is nonlinear: R(S,v)=sum r_i v_i/(1+sum v_j); revenues r_i in [0,1] known to learner
Learner knows the cardinality bound K (here mapped to m)
settings.definition_quote: consider an option space containing $N$ distinct elements ... this selection is given by a Multinomial Logit (MNL) choice model ... minimize the {\it regret} defined as \Reg(T,\mb{v}) = \Ex\left[\sum_{t=1}^T R(S^*,\mb{v}) - R(S_t,\mb{v})\right]

algorithms.name: TS algorithm for MNL-Bandit with Independent Beta priors (Algorithm 1)
TS algorithm for MNL-Bandit with Gaussian approximation and correlated sampling (Algorithm 2)

tuning: K correlated Gaussian samples per epoch

source.label: main_result
source.quote: For any instance $\mb{v} = (v_0, \cdots, v_N)$ of the \banditMNL~problem with $N$ products, $r_i\in [0,1]$, and satisfying Assumption \ref{assumption1}, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{learn_algo_normal} in time $T$ is bounded as, \reg(T,\mb{v}) \leq C_1\sqrt{NT}\log{TK} + C_2N\log^2{TK}, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are absolute constants (independent of problem parameters).

results.notes: C_1, C_2 unspecified absolute constants, so recorded as O. Regret defined via expected revenues, hence pseudo-regret. Paper's K (assortment size) mapped to m; paper's N to N_items. Proof uses T >= N in a step.
